items.followUp: How many seconds are there in 2 years? Write your answer in scientific notation.

rubric.why: Checks the conversion from years to seconds using 365 days per year.
rubric.how: Award for multiplying 365 days, 24 hours, 60 minutes and 60 seconds.

rubric.why: Checks the numerical result and its unit.
rubric.how: Award for 3.1536 × 10^7 seconds, or the equivalent 31,536,000 seconds.

items.followUp: Define average speed and state its SI unit.

rubric.why: Checks the defining feature of constant speed.
rubric.how: Award for stating that speed remains constant, or that equal distances are covered in equal time intervals.

rubric.why: Checks the defining feature of variable speed.
rubric.how: Award for stating that speed changes, or that unequal distances are covered in equal time intervals.

modelAnswer: Constant speed: An object has constant speed when it covers equal distances in equal intervals of time.
Variable speed: An object has variable speed when its speed changes; it covers unequal distances in equal intervals of time.

items.followUp: Define uniform acceleration and give one example of motion with uniform acceleration.

rubric.why: Checks that uniform velocity has constant magnitude and direction.
rubric.how: Award for stating that an object has uniform velocity when it makes equal displacements in equal intervals of time in the same direction.

rubric.why: Checks that the rate of change of velocity is constant.
rubric.how: Award for stating that velocity changes by equal amounts in equal intervals of time.

modelAnswer: Uniform velocity: An object has uniform velocity when it makes equal displacements in equal intervals of time in the same direction.
Uniform acceleration: An object has uniform acceleration when its velocity changes by equal amounts in equal intervals of time.

items.followUp: Why do passengers jerk backward when a bus starts suddenly?

rubric.why: Checks identification of inertia as the cause.
rubric.how: Award for naming inertia, particularly the inertia of motion.

rubric.why: Checks the explanation of the passengers’ forward movement relative to the bus.
rubric.how: Award for explaining that the feet slow with the bus while the upper body tends to keep moving forward.

modelAnswer: When the driver applies brakes suddenly, the bus and the passengers’ feet slow down.
Because of inertia of motion, the upper part of the passengers’ bodies tends to keep moving forward, so they fall forward.

items.followUp: Define the moment of a force and write its SI unit.

rubric.why: Checks the meaning or defining relationship for torque.
rubric.how: Award for defining torque as the turning effect of a force, or as force multiplied by perpendicular distance from the pivot.

modelAnswer: Torque is the turning effect of a force about a pivot or axis.
Torque = force × perpendicular distance from the pivot.
Its SI unit is the newton metre (N m).

items.followUp: When does a force do work? Give the SI unit of work.

rubric.why: Checks that work requires displacement caused by a force in its direction.
rubric.how: Award for stating that work is done when a force causes displacement in the direction of the force.

rubric.why: Checks the SI unit of work.

modelAnswer: Work is done when a force causes an object to move through a displacement in the direction of the force.
The SI unit of work is the joule (J).

items.followUp: Define power and write its equation in terms of energy transferred and time.

rubric.why: Checks the meaning of power as a rate.
rubric.how: Award for defining power as the rate of doing work or transferring energy.
Award for P = W/t, or the equivalent equation using energy transferred.

modelAnswer: Power is the rate of doing work, or the work done per unit time.

items.followUp: Define energy and name the two kinds of mechanical energy.

rubric.how: Award for stating that energy is the capacity or ability to do work.

rubric.why: Checks that both kinds of energy are named.
rubric.how: Award for naming kinetic energy and potential energy.

modelAnswer: Energy is the capacity to do work.
The two kinds of mechanical energy are kinetic energy and potential energy.
